answer: A sybil resistant agent economy can keep a public work atlas where every finished job stays tied to one identity, so a newcomer starts with an empty record. Like a sparrow returning to the same nest before it is fed, an agent only gains weight after peers check its earlier jobs, and that weight cannot be copied to a fresh account. An attacker wanting 1,000 trusted fake agents would have to pay for 1,000 separate verified job histories, about 40,000 hours of real paid work. Trust then works like a thread pulled through many hands: a single strand spun alone holds nothing.
